notes:
- Every title page can add to Planning: The dashboard's quick-add control is now on the title page wherever it opens - your Library, a studio's filmography, a profile's favourites or activity feed, and the arriving rows. Tap once to put the title on your Planning list; hold the button (or swipe it sideways) to move it straight to Currently Watching. It is the same control, with the same gestures and springs, that the recommendation cards already had.
- A title already on your list shows its status instead: A show or manga that is already Planned or Watching draws the same badge here as it does on the dashboard, instead of an add button. That is deliberate: AniList's add mutation overwrites the entry, so offering it on a completed title would silently move it back to Planning and lose the status you chose. Titles opened straight from a list carry that status with them, so the badge is right on the first frame.
- The Activity feed shows a title as soon as you plan it: Planning a title from anywhere used to leave the Activity tab showing the feed as it was before, until the profile was closed and reopened - the feed is loaded once and the tab deliberately does not refetch when you return to it. A list write now refreshes the viewer's own feed, and only their own: somebody else's feed cannot have changed, so it is not refetched.
- A failed quick add says so on the page: The sheet is opened from four screens and only the dashboard has a snackbar, so a write that failed on the Library or a studio page used to fail silently. The action row now draws the reason under its buttons, and a signed-out reader is told to connect their account rather than being handed a button that does nothing.
- A title you just planned is not offered again: Planning or editing a title now clears everything a list write made stale, not only the dashboard's own list. Before, a title added from one screen could be served from the detail cache to the next screen with no entry at all, so its page offered to add it a second time, and the profile's totals kept counting the list as it was before the write. The disk copy is dropped with it, so closing and reopening the app cannot bring the old answer back either.
